name: Dmitriusz Achebe-Svensson
subcategory: augmented combat / Titan Compact Premier League
description: Dmitriusz Achebe-Svensson is the most controversial active fighter in the Titan Compact Premier League, a Polish-Igbo-Swedish augmented combat specialist whose chrome package — licensed by Axiom Workforce Solutions as an 'industrial-grade occupational chassis' rather than sports equipment — sits in a regulatory gray zone that the league has been litigating for three seasons. His right arm is a military-adjacent hydraulic assembly that delivers impact forces the league's safety guidelines do not formally classify, and four of his last seven opponents have required post-bout surgical reconstruction. He is currently ranked first in the Premier League standings and is under investigation by two separate Meridian district oversight bodies.
story_hooks: One of his surgically reconstructed opponents is willing to testify that pre-bout officials measured his arm assembly and cleared it under pressure from a Titan Compact executive with documented Axiom financial ties.

Achebe-Svensson privately approaches a Tier 2 legal advocacy group — he wants out of his Axiom contract and believes the chassis installed in him contains monitoring hardware that was never disclosed.

A Tier 1 community organizer who knew Dmitriusz before his recruitment is building a case that his original labor contract contained coercive clauses that made the combat pathway effectively unavoidable — a form of debt-bonded augmentation.
